chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from al-Aḥwal, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh: I come out from the privy and cleanse myself with water, then my garment falls into that water with which I performed istinjāʾ. So he said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْخَلَاءِ: the privy or place of relieving oneself
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الَّذِي اسْتَنْجَيْتُ بِهِ: the water with which post-relief cleansing was performed
key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: with water, the medium used for purification here
key_terms.فَأَسْتَنْجِي: I cleanse myself after relieving myself using water
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is not problematic

ai.seo_question: Does water used for istinjāʾ make a garment impure if it touches it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding water used for istinjāʾ and contact with one’s garment. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if the garment falls into that water, there is no problem in it, indicating permissibility and the absence of impurity in this case.
